semantic.name: Text Muted
semantic.notes: Hard General Text rule: use the weakest Neutral foreground that still clears the 4.5:1 minimum against the actual normal context. Do not strengthen Muted merely to chase 7:1.
semantic.context: Normal context within the active mode.
semantic.sourceRule: Neutral scale only, inside the legal readable hierarchy band for this mode/context.
semantic.appearanceRule: Weakest viable readable foreground; pass minimum while staying visibly quieter than Subtle.
semantic.relationshipRule: Muted is the weakest readable level that still passes; do not strengthen it merely to chase the recommended ratio.

semantic.name: Text Subtle
semantic.notes: Hard General Text rule: choose a perceptual middle ground between Muted and Default with meaningful visual distinction from both. Minimum contrast 4.5:1.

semantic.sourceRule: Neutral scale only, inside the legal readable hierarchy band for this mode/context.
semantic.appearanceRule: Middle readable foreground; clearly stronger than Muted and quieter than Default.
semantic.relationshipRule: Subtle sits perceptually between Muted and Default and must be meaningfully distinct from both.

semantic.relationshipRule: Subtle sits perceptually between Muted and Default and must be meaningfully distinct from both.

semantic.name: Text Primary

semantic.name: Canvas Primary

global: Semantic Colour maps existing roles to existing approved Primitive colours only; never invent raw colours or new roles.

Treat accessibilityMinimum as a hard requirement where present. Treat accessibilityRecommended as a preferred target only after hierarchy and family character are protected; a minimum-passing family-faithful colour is preferable to a recommended-ratio colour that visibly loses its identity.
Prefer the weakest/closest viable colour that satisfies the role. Do not jump unnecessarily towards Neutral 0/100 or the deepest/lightest ramp extreme just to maximise contrast.
Keep neighbouring hierarchy levels perceptually distinct. Muted, Subtle, Default, Strong and Bold must not collapse into visually near-identical choices.
Preserve the intended colour family and mode character. Solve accessibility inside the legal family/band wherever possible.
Light and Dark are independently resolved Semantic modes. Inverse roles represent the opposing context within the active mode.

Text: General readable text must meet its hard contrast minimum against the representative normal/inverse Surface.
Muted is the weakest readable level that still passes; do not strengthen it merely to chase the recommended ratio.
Subtle sits perceptually between Muted and Default and must be meaningfully distinct from both.
Default is the primary general foreground and may use the stronger end of Neutral where appropriate.

Chromatic Base text is literal in Light mode. In Dark mode it may move only towards lighter tones within the same family when the literal Base cannot clear 4.5:1 against the normal dark Surface Strong; prefer the nearest readable family-preserving tone rather than an endpoint.

Family Strong and Strong Inverse variants must satisfy the hard accessibility minimum and meaningful Base separation (hard-minimum ΔE 5, preferred ΔE 7+). Once the minimum contrast is met, preserve recognisable hue/chroma and cross-family distinction before chasing the 7:1 recommendation. A 4.5–6.99:1 family-preserving Strong is a valid PASS and should beat a 7:1+ option that becomes muddy, generic or too similar to another family.
Fill: Fill is decorative/structural colour material rather than text contrast by itself; do not show a contrast requirement unless a specific component contract adds one.
Maintain the five-level hierarchy Subtle → Soft → Base → Strong → Bold with clear perceptual separation.

Light-mode chromatic Fill Base is fixed to the approved family base. Dark-mode Fill is purpose-led across the same family: build a visible Subtle → Soft → Base → Strong → Bold hierarchy and allow Base to move when the literal source would make the material disappear or break the hierarchy.
Avoid pushing Subtle so close to the surrounding Surface that it disappears, or Bold so close to black/white that family character is lost.
Border: Subtle borders are low-emphasis decorative separators and do not carry the shared non-text contrast rule.
Base, Strong and Bold borders are meaningful boundaries and must meet the hard non-text contrast minimum where specified.
Keep Subtle < Base < Strong < Bold perceptually ordered and visibly separated.
Prefer the least extreme family tone that meets the required boundary contrast; do not make every border Bold-equivalent.
Surface: Surface is contained UI background material. Ground is reserved for Canvas and must not be used as Surface.
General Primary/Secondary/Tertiary are Neutral-derived and should remain close enough to feel related but distinct enough to create usable layering.
In Light mode, a normal Surface resolves towards a light, restrained background material and Strong resolves towards a dark opposing background; Dark mode mirrors that polarity for the active theme.

Surface selection is source-adaptive: preserve recognisable family character without clinging to the base when the base is unsuitable as background material, and avoid pushing either role towards white/black merely to maximise tonal distance.
Strong surfaces are opposing/high-emphasis counterparts and must remain clearly distinct from both their normal partner and the raw family base where the palette allows.

Identity and Status surfaces use restrained family material so content can sit on them without the surface becoming visually overwhelming; a very dark source may legitimately use a slight tint for the dark-side Surface when further shading would only collapse it towards black.
Canvas: Canvas is large-scale page/structural background material and may use only Ground source families.
Ground is Canvas-only. Studio generates Ground Tint/Shade families deterministically from the three supplied Ground source colours.
Light and Dark Canvas roles are resolved independently by purpose and luminance; never mechanically swap Primary and Tertiary.
Light Canvas roles must remain genuinely light; Dark Canvas roles must remain genuinely dark.
Primary, Secondary and Tertiary should remain visibly distinct where the Ground families allow it.
Light and Dark Canvas are separate semantic environments, not index-swapped versions of one another.
Dedicated Dark Ground is optional. If any Dark Ground anchor is supplied, all three must be supplied before Studio uses that set.
When dedicated Dark Ground is absent, Studio may derive Dark Canvas from generated Light Ground families.
Ground remains Canvas-only; Surface must never source Ground.
Interaction: Interaction colours are direct-purpose Primitive sources for links, visited links, focus and related control states.

Links/visited links must meet their text contrast requirement against the representative background; when colour alone distinguishes a link from surrounding text, also maintain meaningful distinction from that text or provide a non-colour cue.
Focus indicators must meet the non-text contrast minimum against adjacent colours.
Placeholder text must meet the text contrast requirement where the contract specifies it.
Tones / Design Material: Tones expose the approved Primary/Secondary/Accent/Neutral design material directly; they are not independently generated Semantic colours.
Use them as flexible design material while respecting component-level accessibility when applied.

selectionEngine.accessibility: Hard minimums are gates only where the role defines a minimum. Recommended ratios are preferences, never a reason to flatten hierarchy.
selectionEngine.hierarchy: Related roles are selected as coherent sequences rather than independently. Adjacent levels must remain perceptually ordered and separated.
selectionEngine.perception: Use OKLab/OKLCH evidence. Penalise chromatic candidates that collapse towards white/black or lose most family chroma when a healthier legal option exists.
selectionEngine.endpoints: Avoid Neutral 0/100 and deepest/lightest family endpoints unless role purpose or hard contrast genuinely requires them.
selectionEngine.families: Preserve Primary, Secondary, Accent and Status identity. Check like-for-like cross-family roles for visual collision.
selectionEngine.fallback: If Local AI is unavailable or returns unusable output, use BufferCore's highest-scoring deterministic coherent option.
